To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the ubiquitination of the cancer/testis antigen NY-ESO1 on non-lysines is a prerequisite for its processing and presentation by MHC class I; (ii) the regulation of NY-EOS-1 processing by ubiquitin receptors and the proteasome is governed via non-canonical ubiquitin linkages; (iii) the ubiquitinated NY-EOS- 1 protein is degraded by the proteasome and the immunoproteasomes.

1) the NY-ES0-1 cancer/testes antigen is degraded by the proteasome via a non-lysine ubiquitination pathway; 2) Rpn10 and/or Rpn13 regulate the supply of the HLA-A2-restricted NY- ES0-1157– 165 antigen by binding to the non-lysine modified NY-ESO1; 3) the immunoproteasomes are involved in NY-ESO processing.
the processing of a non-lysine ubiquitinated antigen is governed by non-lysine receptors and proteasomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in the processing of the cancer/testis antigen NY-ESO1.
the regulation of MHC class-I-restricted peptide generation.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that govern the processing of cancer antigens for the generation of MHC class-I-restricted peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
at least in this case, ubiquitination of NY-ES0-1 is not required for MHC class I presentation.
the ubiquitination of NY-ESOs-1 is not required for its processing by the standard and the immunoproteasomes.
non-lysine ubiquitination of the cancer/testis antigen NY-ESO1 is a prerequisite for its efficient MHC class I processing and presentation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
non-lysine ubiquitination is important for antigen processing.
the ubiquitination of NY-ES0-1 by non-lysine residues is important for its processing by the 26S proteasome, and that Rpn10/Rpn13 and the proteasomes are important for its processing.
ubiquitination on NY-ESO1 regulates the supply of the NY- ESO-1 1157–165 epitope for presentation by MHC class I molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
non-lysine ubiquitination is an important mechanism for the generation of MHC class 1 antigenic epitopes.

the ubiquitination of NY-ES0-1 on non-lysines, which is not recognized by Rpn10, is required to allow for the efficient processing and presentation of the NY- ES0-1-derived HLA-A* 0201-restricted antigenic peptide.

non-canonical ubiquitin linkages and attachment sites can be used to regulate the processing of a cancer/testis antigen by the proteasome and that this regulation involves the Rpn10 and the Rpn13 ubiquitin receptors.
